Step 3 has the reader press Shift+Tab to leave plan mode, which can land in Manual mode, where every file write asks first. The pilot Try in Grilling trains the opposite habit with "If it asks permission to create or edit a file, choose No". reader.problem: "Read the spec and ticket files in the `.scratch` folder" can't be done as written by a reader who knows only a terminal. The folder name starts with a dot, so Finder and `ls` hide it by default, the feature subfolder's name isn't known in advance, and nothing says how to open a file. The line "Don't `/clear` before this point" also comes after all the work that needed the window.
reader.evidence: Line 247: "Read the spec and ticket files in the `.scratch` folder. Don't `/clear` before this point." The local tracker writes `.scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md`, where the agent picks the slug.
reader.fix: Replace step 8 with: "Ask the agent: 'List every file you wrote under .scratch and show me spec.md.' (Or open a second terminal window, `cd todo-practice`, and run `ls -R .scratch` then `cat .scratch/*/spec.md`. The dot at the start of the name hides the folder in Finder.) If it offers to start building, say no, or press Esc to stop it. Type `/exit` when you're done." Then put the clearing rule into step 5: "Do steps 5 to 7 in this one conversation. Don't type `/clear` until the end."

Remove the outcome sentence and state the edges, so the 'edges' distractor has something to act on:
```test spot-horizontal
Lee approved this breakdown for a booking site: 01 every database table, 02 every API route, 03 every screen, each blocked by the one before. Spot the mistake.
- [ ] Too few tickets: it should have been twelve smaller ones.
  > More layer tickets would make it worse. The problem is the direction of the cut.
- [x] Each ticket is one layer, so nothing can be tried until 03 lands.
  > Right. Horizontal slices push all feedback to the end. A tracer bullet runs through every layer and can be tried on its own.
- [ ] The tickets needed file paths and line numbers so agents could find the code.
  > Tickets avoid file paths because they go stale. The cut was the problem.
- [ ] 03 should be blocked by nothing, so the screens can start at once.
  > Screens with nothing behind them still can't be tried. Changing the edges doesn't fix a cut by layer.
```

quiz.fix:
Replace it with a transfer scenario. Ids become permanent only once published, and this rewrite isn't live yet:
```test scenario-near-smart-zone
Grilling a podcast-site feature ran long. It's settled and needs several sessions to build, and you're close to the edge of the Smart zone. You haven't typed `/to-spec` yet. What next?
- [ ] `/clear`, then `/to-spec` in the fresh, empty session.
  > Clearing empties the conversation `/to-spec` writes from. Every decision you just made would be gone.
- [ ] Push on: type `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets` straight away, before the room runs out.
  > Near the edge of the Smart zone the agent reasons less sharply, so the spec and tickets come out sloppier. Don't push on degraded.
- [x] `/compact` now, at the end of grilling, then type `/to-spec`.
  > Right. `/compact` keeps a summary of the decisions and frees room. Do it at a phase boundary, like the end of grilling.
- [ ] Skip the spec and `/implement` the whole feature in this session.
  > It needs several sessions, and this one is nearly full. That's exactly when a spec and tickets earn their keep.
```

quiz.problem: Two distractors repeat one misconception: (a) 'should have typed /clear between them' and (d) 'should only ever run in a new session'. Option b is a straw man that no reader would pick ('seams only matter to experts'). The right answer also states as fact what happens next ('the spec went in with the agent's guess'). That happened in the author's own session, but the Skill doesn't guarantee it. The mistake itself is leaving the question unanswered.

quiz.fix:
```test spot-seam-skip
While `/to-spec` was waiting for an answer about which seams to test at, Sam typed `/to-tickets` to keep things moving. Spot the mistake.
- [ ] Sam should have typed `/clear` between the two Skills.
  > Clearing before `/to-tickets` breaks the one-window rule. The problem was the unanswered question.
- [ ] Nothing: the agent's own guess at the seams is usually good enough.
  > Seams decide where `/tdd` writes tests and what `/code-review` checks against. They're yours to agree, not the agent's to guess.
- [x] Sam never agreed the seams, so the agent had to guess them.
  > Right. The seam check is the one moment `/to-spec` waits for you. Answer it before typing the next Skill.
- [ ] Seams belong in the tickets, so Sam can agree them when `/to-tickets` asks.
  > `/to-tickets` never asks about seams, and its templates have no field for them. The spec is where they get agreed.
```
(Accurate per to-tickets SKILL.md: the quiz step asks about granularity, edges and merge/split only, and the local template has no seam field. Right answer is 58 chars; d is the longest.)

acc-skills.problem: On a real tracker the Lesson says `/to-tickets` "uses the tracker's own blocking links and files each ticket under the spec's issue", with no conditions. Native links are used only where the tracker has them; otherwise "Blocked by" goes in the issue text.

acc-skills.problem: The worked example doesn't follow the Lesson's own seam advice. `/to-spec` proposes two seams, one of them new, and the user says "Yes, both" without asking whether one would do.
